children: Americans received plenty of cautionary messages this week, covering housing, government spending, monetary policy, war costs and the stock market. Here are five stories that shaped the conversation.
Kevin O’Leary Urges Caution Before Buying A Home
Investor
Kevin O’Leary
advised Americans to think carefully before taking on mortgage debt, saying job stability and financial security should come before homeownership.
He suggested renting first to evaluate a neighborhood and confirm that income can reliably support the commitment.
Read the full article
Elizabeth Warren Questions The Results Of The Iran War
Sen.
Elizabeth Warren
(D-Mass.) questioned what the U.S. has accomplished in the nearly eight-month war with Iran, saying it has killed as many as 23 U.S. service members and cost more than $45 billion.
Pentagon data listed 21 deaths and 865 wounded as of Oct. 10.
Read the full article

Kevin Warsh Acknowledges Shortcomings At The Federal Reserve
Fed Chairman
Kevin Warsh
said he failed to give enough attention to nonmonetary duties, including bank supervision, during his first 148 days in office.
He made the remarks to IMF chief
Kristalina Georgieva
at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings on Oct. 16.
Read the full article
Peter Schiff Raises The Prospect Of A Pre-Midterm Market Crash
Veteran investor
Peter Schiff
warned that stocks could crash before the midterms, citing inflation, a weak economy and tougher financing for the AI boom.
"Remember, this is October," he said on X, pointing also to sharply higher Treasury yields and a softer labor market.
Read the full article
Rand Paul Calls For Spending Cuts And A Balanced Budget
Sen.
Rand Paul
(R-Ky.) called for sweeping cuts in federal spending, arguing the U.S. cannot sustain its fiscal path with national debt above $40 trillion.
He said government-funded benefits are not free, since taxpayers ultimately cover the cost.
